problem:
Suppose we wish to approximate the solution to an initial value problem using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

If the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)=3{x}^{2}+5x,$ find an expression for the local truncation error for the step from $x$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx.$
worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a single step of a numerical method, when the step begins from an exact value. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value ${y}_{\text{exact}}$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact solution of the initial value problem is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)=3{x}^{2}+5x.$ Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method.

First, the slope at a step starting at $x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(x)=(3{x}^{2}+5x)^{′}=6x+5.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the increment given by the numerical method is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(x)\cdot Δx \\  & =(6x+5)\cdot Δx.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at ${x}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & =({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δx) \\  & =3(x+Δx)^{2}+5(x+Δx) \\  & =3({x}^{2}+2x\cdot Δx+(Δx)^{2})+5x+5\cdot Δx \\  & =3{x}^{2}+6x\cdot Δx+3\cdot (Δx)^{2}+5x+5\cdot Δx \\  & =3{x}^{2}+(6x+5)\cdot Δx+3\cdot (Δx)^{2}+5x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for step $n$ starting at $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy) \\  & =[3{x}^{2}+(6x+5)\cdot Δx+3\cdot (Δx)^{2}+5x]-[3{x}^{2}+5x+(6x+5)\cdot Δx] \\  & =3{x}^{2}-3{x}^{2}+((6x+5)-(6x+5))\cdot Δx+5x-5x+3\cdot (Δx)^{2} \\  & =3\cdot (Δx)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
